newsitem.title: UK: LME monitoring copper market closely - King.
newsitem.headline: LME monitoring copper market closely - King.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange (LME) is monitoring its copper market closely, particularly with regard to the backwardation on the nearby dates, LME Chief Executive David King said.
"The Executive of the LME, as you would expect, is monitoring the copper market Very closely at present," King said.
King said that the LME was looking at the copper market, "particularly against the background of the backwardation structure in the nearby dates."

The LME copper market is currently in the grip of a fierce technical squeeze, with the cash to three months backwardation or spot premium currently at $300/310. On Tuesday, this spread reached $330/340.
The tightness is particularly acute nearby, with premiums of $24 paid on Tuesday to borrow copper for one day. This is close to the limit the LME allows for daily backwardations at present.
The tightness in the market reflects large speculative shorts from an autumn-1996 sell-off becoming prompt, with a European merchant said to be the major long-holder, traders said.
